Donald Trump keeps figuring out new ways to shock people on social media, but a comment he made Friday about Russian president Vladimir Putin was in another league altogether.

The president held a press conference on Friday, a day after he met Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, and was asked about his relationship with the Russian leader.

CNN’s Kaitlan Collins — a popular Trump target — noted that, while in China, Trump said Putin was his “friend,” before noting that Russia is Iran’s biggest ally.

“Do you believe Putin is a friend to America?” she asked bluntly.

In response, Trump seemed to suggest that it’s none of America’s concern what people think of his relationship with Putin.

“I can’t speak to America. I’ve been dealing with Putin during the fake ‘Russia, Russia, Russia’ hoax. And to be honest, he was very nice about it,” Trump said, before adding that he considers the Russian president “somebody that I have a very good relationship [with].”

Trump then appeared to sympathize with Putin for getting into a war with Ukraine, which he said, ”should have lasted one day and it’s lasted for five years.”

ABC News reporter Rachel Scott continued the questioning, and Trump freely admitted he’s “so nice to Russia,” stressing, “It’s a good thing that I have a relationship,” insisting that, “You’re very lucky to have somebody that has a relationship with the heads of the most powerful countries.”

You can see the exchange below.

HuffPost reached out to the White House for comment, but no one immediately responded.

Not surprisingly, many people on social media were aghast at Trump’s comments, with some suggesting that he cares more about a Russian president than his own citizens.
